Data dictionary

Columns, event types, info fields, versions and joins of the OPDI files of release v2.0.0.

Release v2.0.0 is the upcoming release: its files are being produced, starting with the days from 1 January 2025. The data available today are those of release v0.0.2, described on Release v0.0.2.

Every column, event type and info field of the OPDI files of release v2.0.0 (default settings of the OPDI software), with the version columns and joins. For what is published, see the overview. The column tables come from the software’s own list of published columns, so they always match the files.

How to read the tables

  • Type: string (text), double (decimal), boolean (true or false), date or timestamp (date and time).
  • Unit: every time is in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). Altitudes are in feet (ft), distances in nautical miles (NM, 1 NM = 1,852 m), durations in seconds (s) or minutes (min), angles in degrees.
  • An empty value (NULL) means the item was not detected or is not known. It never stands for zero.

Flight list

One row per flight. The file of a day holds the flights first seen on that day (UTC). A flight here is a track: the position reports of one aircraft that OPDI treats as one flight (see Tracks and flight identity).

Column Type Unit Description
flight_id string Unique identifier of the flight. A flight is one track: the sequence of position reports of one aircraft that belong together.
icao24 string ICAO 24-bit address of the aircraft’s transponder, written as six hexadecimal characters. It normally stays with one aircraft.
flt_id string Call sign broadcast by the aircraft, for example DLH123.
dof date UTC Date of the flight: the day on which it was first seen. A day’s files hold the flights of that date.
adep string Departure airport, as its four-letter ICAO code. ‘OOA’ (out of area) when the track began at the edge of the covered area, so the flight departed from somewhere outside it. This occurs only in data built with European coverage. NULL when no departure airport could be identified, which includes every overflight.
ades string Destination airport, as its four-letter ICAO code. ‘OOA’ (out of area) when the track ended at the edge of the covered area, so the flight continued to somewhere outside it. This occurs only in data built with European coverage. NULL when no destination airport could be identified, which includes every overflight.
adep_p string Other airports near the start of the track that the flight could have left from, as a comma-separated list of ICAO codes, nearest first.
ades_p string Other airports near the end of the track that the flight could have gone to, as a comma-separated list of ICAO codes, nearest first.
adep_source string How the departure airport was decided. ‘aerodrome’: adep names the airport near which the track began, found from the position and height of its first reports. ‘runway_event’: adep was taken from a take-off detected on one of that airport’s runways, which takes precedence over the first method. ‘out_of_area’: adep is ‘OOA’. ‘undetermined’: no airport could be identified and adep is NULL, as for an overflight.
ades_source string How the destination airport was decided, with the same four values as adep_source: ‘aerodrome’ (found from the last reports of the track), ‘runway_event’ (taken from a landing detected on one of the airport’s runways), ‘out_of_area’ (ades is ‘OOA’) and ‘undetermined’ (ades is NULL).
registration string Registration of the aircraft (its tail number), from the OpenSky aircraft database. NULL when the aircraft is not in that database.
model string Aircraft model, from the OpenSky aircraft database.
typecode string ICAO aircraft type designator, for example A320, from the OpenSky aircraft database.
icao_aircraft_class string ICAO aircraft description, for example L2J for a landplane with two jet engines, from the OpenSky aircraft database.
icao_operator string Three-letter ICAO code of the aircraft operator, from the OpenSky aircraft database.
first_seen timestamp UTC Time of the first position report of the flight received by the OpenSky Network.
last_seen timestamp UTC Time of the last position report of the flight received by the OpenSky Network.
atot timestamp UTC Actual take-off time: when the aircraft left the runway at the departure airport. Taken from the flight’s earliest ATOT event at that airport. NULL when no take-off was detected.
aldt timestamp UTC Actual landing time: when the aircraft touched down at the destination airport. Taken from the flight’s latest ALDT event at that airport. NULL when no landing was detected.
aobt timestamp UTC Actual off-block time: when the aircraft started to move away from its parking position. Taken from the flight’s earliest AOBT event. NULL when it was not detected, which is common because it needs reception on the ground.
aibt timestamp UTC Actual in-block time: when the aircraft stopped at its parking position after landing. Taken from the flight’s latest AIBT event. NULL when it was not detected, which is common because it needs reception on the ground.
rwy_dep string Runway used for take-off, for example 25R. Taken from the same event as atot.
rwy_dep_bearing_deg double degrees True bearing of the centre line of the take-off runway, in degrees clockwise from north. It describes the runway, not the heading of the aircraft.
rwy_arr string Runway used for landing, for example 07L. Taken from the same event as aldt.
rwy_arr_bearing_deg double degrees True bearing of the centre line of the landing runway, in degrees clockwise from north. It describes the runway, not the heading of the aircraft.
stnd_dep string Parking position (stand) the flight left from, with the name it has in OpenStreetMap. NULL when it was not detected.
stnd_arr string Parking position (stand) the flight arrived at, with the name it has in OpenStreetMap. NULL when it was not detected.
c40_arr timestamp UTC Time when the arriving flight last crossed, inbound, a circle of 40 nautical miles (NM) radius around the destination airport. NULL when no such crossing was detected.
c50_arr timestamp UTC Time when the arriving flight last crossed, inbound, a circle of 50 nautical miles (NM) radius around the destination airport. NULL when no such crossing was detected.
c60_arr timestamp UTC Time when the arriving flight last crossed, inbound, a circle of 60 nautical miles (NM) radius around the destination airport. NULL when no such crossing was detected.
c100_arr timestamp UTC Time when the arriving flight last crossed, inbound, a circle of 100 nautical miles (NM) radius around the destination airport. NULL when no such crossing was detected.
c110_arr timestamp UTC Time when the arriving flight last crossed, inbound, a circle of 110 nautical miles (NM) radius around the destination airport. NULL when no such crossing was detected.
c120_arr timestamp UTC Time when the arriving flight last crossed, inbound, a circle of 120 nautical miles (NM) radius around the destination airport. NULL when no such crossing was detected.
c40_dep timestamp UTC Time when the departing flight first crossed, outbound, a circle of 40 nautical miles (NM) radius around the departure airport. NULL when no such crossing was detected.
c50_dep timestamp UTC Time when the departing flight first crossed, outbound, a circle of 50 nautical miles (NM) radius around the departure airport. NULL when no such crossing was detected.
c60_dep timestamp UTC Time when the departing flight first crossed, outbound, a circle of 60 nautical miles (NM) radius around the departure airport. NULL when no such crossing was detected.
c100_dep timestamp UTC Time when the departing flight first crossed, outbound, a circle of 100 nautical miles (NM) radius around the departure airport. NULL when no such crossing was detected.
c110_dep timestamp UTC Time when the departing flight first crossed, outbound, a circle of 110 nautical miles (NM) radius around the departure airport. NULL when no such crossing was detected.
c120_dep timestamp UTC Time when the departing flight first crossed, outbound, a circle of 120 nautical miles (NM) radius around the departure airport. NULL when no such crossing was detected.
track_duration_min double min Time between first_seen and last_seen, in minutes. Very short tracks are often pieces of a flight seen on the ground rather than whole flights. No row is removed on this value, so users can choose their own limit.
superseded_dep boolean True when this row is a piece of a departure that is already counted on another row: it has no take-off, and the same aircraft departs again from the same airport within 3 hours (10,800 s). False otherwise.
superseded_arr boolean True when this row is a piece of an arrival that is already counted on another row: it has no landing, and the same aircraft arrived at the same airport within the 3 hours (10,800 s) before. False otherwise.
movement_dep boolean True when this row counts as a departure: the row names an airport, it is not a fragment counted on another row, and there is evidence that the aircraft flew (a detected runway time, an airport at the other end, or a crossing of one of the distance circles). Use this column to count departures.
movement_arr boolean True when this row counts as an arrival: the row names an airport, it is not a fragment counted on another row, and there is evidence that the aircraft flew (a detected runway time, an airport at the other end, or a crossing of one of the distance circles). Use this column to count arrivals.
version string Version of the method that built this flight row, for example v5.0.0. It changes only when that method changes.
release string Name of the data release the row belongs to (v2.0.0). It is the same on every row of a release.

How the airports were found

adep_source and ades_source say how the departure and destination airport were found, with one of four values; Departure and destination airports explains each case.

  • aerodrome: An airport was named from the trajectory: from the first position (departure) or the descent near an airport (destination).
  • out_of_area: Departure only: the track began in the air near the edge of the area covered, so the flight came from outside it. Not used when the area covered is the whole world.
  • undetermined: No airport could be named.
  • runway_event: The airport was taken from a take-off or landing detected on a runway, replacing the value found from the trajectory.

Flight events

An event is a moment in a flight, with a time and a position. One row per event, in three parts:

  1. the columns of the event, in the table below;
  2. the measurement columns;
  3. the columns of the event’s flight, as in the flight list (flight_id appears once, among the event columns; the flight’s version is flight_version, see Versions).
Column Type Unit Description
event_id string Unique identifier of the event.
flight_id string Identifier of the flight the event belongs to. It matches flight_id in the flight list.
type string Event type, for example ATOT, level-start or xing-40nm. The data dictionary lists every type.
event_time timestamp UTC Time at which the event happened.
longitude double degrees Longitude of the aircraft at the event, in degrees (WGS 84, positive east).
latitude double degrees Latitude of the aircraft at the event, in degrees (WGS 84, positive north).
altitude_ft double ft Altitude of the aircraft at the event, in feet, from the barometric altitude the aircraft reports. For a flight-level crossing it is the flight level times 100. NULL for events that have no altitude.
h3_res_5 string Cell of the H3 hexagonal grid at resolution 5 that contains the event position. Cells cover about 250 km2 each, so the column can be used to select events in a region quickly.
source string Source of the position reports, OSN for the OpenSky Network.
version string Version of the method that produced this event type, for example events_v0.4.0. Different event types can have different versions.
info string Extra details about the event, as JSON text, for example the runway or the airport. The keys depend on the event type and are listed in the data dictionary.
flight_version string Version of the method that built the flight’s row in the flight list (the version column of the flight list).
release string Name of the data release the row belongs to (v2.0.0). It is the same on every row of a release.

Every published event has a time. Events the aircraft’s own track clearly contradicts, such as an in-block time while it is still flying, are not published.

Measurements

A measurement is a number attached to an event, stored as a column of the flight events file and empty where it does not apply (see Empty measurement columns).

Column Type Unit Description
distance_flown_nm double NM Distance flown from the start of the track to this event, along the received positions, in nautical miles (NM, 1 NM = 1,852 m).
time_passed_s double s Time from the first position of the track to this event, in seconds.
holding_duration_s double s Time spent in a holding pattern, in seconds. A holding pattern is a loop flown while the aircraft waits for permission to continue. It is set only on holding-end events and is NULL on every other event.
holding_distance_nm double NM Distance flown in the holding pattern, in nautical miles (NM). It is set only on holding-end events and is NULL on every other event.
holding_circuits double count Number of loops flown in the holding pattern: the total turn divided by 360 degrees, to one decimal. It is set only on holding-end events and is NULL on every other event.
pms_leg_time_s double s Time spent on a point merge leg, in seconds. A point merge system is an arrival procedure in which aircraft fly along an arc, called a leg, at a fixed distance from a merge point until they are sent directly to it. It is set only on pms-leg-exit events and is NULL on every other event.
pms_leg_distance_nm double NM Distance flown along the point merge leg, in nautical miles (NM). It is set only on pms-leg-exit events and is NULL on every other event.
pms_direct_to_distance_nm double NM Distance from the aircraft to the merge point when it left the leg, in nautical miles (NM). It is set only on pms-leg-exit events and is NULL on every other event.

Computed as in Distance flown, Time passed, Holding patterns and Point merge.

Flight index and catalogue

Flight index

One file per month, index/flight_index_YYYYMM.parquet, with one row per flight of the month. It tells which daily file holds a flight.

Column Type Unit Description
flight_id string Unique identifier of the flight. A flight is one track: the sequence of position reports of one aircraft that belong together.
icao24 string ICAO 24-bit address of the aircraft’s transponder, written as six hexadecimal characters. It normally stays with one aircraft.
flt_id string Call sign broadcast by the aircraft, for example DLH123.
adep string Departure airport, as its four-letter ICAO code. ‘OOA’ (out of area) when the track began at the edge of the covered area, so the flight departed from somewhere outside it. This occurs only in data built with European coverage. NULL when no departure airport could be identified, which includes every overflight.
ades string Destination airport, as its four-letter ICAO code. ‘OOA’ (out of area) when the track ended at the edge of the covered area, so the flight continued to somewhere outside it. This occurs only in data built with European coverage. NULL when no destination airport could be identified, which includes every overflight.
first_seen timestamp UTC Time of the first position report of the flight received by the OpenSky Network.
last_seen timestamp UTC Time of the last position report of the flight received by the OpenSky Network.
dof date UTC Date of the flight: the day on which it was first seen. A day’s files hold the flights of that date.
file string Path of the flight list file that holds the flight, relative to the published folder, for example flight_list/flight_list_20260614.parquet.

Catalogue

One file, catalogue.parquet, with one row per published day.

Column Type Unit Description
day date UTC Day the row describes.
flights bigint count Number of rows in the day’s flight list file.
events bigint count Number of rows in the day’s flight events file.
first_event timestamp UTC Time of the earliest event in the day’s flight events file. NULL when the file is empty.
last_event timestamp UTC Time of the latest event in the day’s flight events file. It can fall on the next day, because a flight keeps all its events in the file of the day it started. NULL when the file is empty.
flight_list_bytes bigint bytes Size of the day’s flight list file.
flight_events_bytes bigint bytes Size of the day’s flight events file.
release string Name of the data release (v2.0.0).
flight_list_version string Version of the flight list method used for the day. When several were used, they are listed separated by commas.
event_versions array Versions of the event methods found in the day’s flight events file.
commit string Identifier of the version of the OPDI software (the git commit) that published the day.
published_at timestamp UTC Time when the day was published.

Event types

type names what an event is. A name with a part in braces stands for a family: xing-fl{level} covers xing-fl50, xing-fl70, xing-fl100 and xing-fl245. Each row links to the page on how the event is found and how accurate it is.

Take-off and landing

  • take-off-roll: The aircraft starts its take-off run. Line-up and take-off roll
  • ATOT: Actual take-off time: the wheels leave the runway. Take-off and landing times
  • xing-runway-threshold: The aircraft passes the runway threshold (the start of the landing part of the runway), a few seconds before touchdown. Runway threshold crossing
  • ALDT: Actual landing time: the wheels touch the runway. Take-off and landing times

Other runway events

  • line-up: A departing aircraft enters the runway to take off. Line-up and take-off roll
  • runway-vacated: An arriving aircraft leaves the runway after landing. Runway vacated
  • runway-crossing-entry: A taxiing aircraft enters a runway to cross it. Runway crossings
  • runway-crossing-vacated: The same aircraft leaves the runway on the other side. Runway crossings
  • go-around: An approaching aircraft gives up the landing and climbs away; placed at the lowest point of the approach. Go-around

Block times

  • AOBT: Actual off-block time: the aircraft starts to move away from its parking position (stand). Off-block and in-block times
  • AIBT: Actual in-block time: the aircraft stops at its stand after landing. Off-block and in-block times

Airport surface

  • entry-{element}: The aircraft enters an area of the airport. {element} is taxiway, apron, parking_position (a stand), threshold, hangar or deicing_pad, for example entry-taxiway. Airport surface events
  • exit-{element}: The aircraft leaves that area, for example exit-parking_position. Airport surface events

Vertical profile

  • top-of-climb: End of the climb to cruise, with the method of EUROCONTROL’s vertical flight efficiency indicators. Top of climb and top of descent
  • top-of-descent: Start of the final descent, same method. Top of climb and top of descent
  • level-start: Start of a period of level flight, cruise included. Level segments
  • level-end: End of that period. Level segments
  • level-off-climb-start: Start of a level-off during the climb: level flight below the cruise. Level-offs
  • level-off-climb-end: End of that level-off. Level-offs
  • level-off-descent-start: Start of a level-off during the descent. Level-offs
  • level-off-descent-end: End of that level-off. Level-offs
  • xing-fl{level}: A crossing of flight level 50, 70, 100 or 245, up or down. Flight-level crossings

A flight level is an altitude in hundreds of feet on the standard air pressure of 1013.25 hPa: level 100 is about 10,000 ft.

Distance rings

  • xing-{radius}nm: A crossing of a circle of 40, 50, 60, 100, 110 or 120 NM around the flight’s departure or destination airport (xing-40nm to xing-120nm). Distance circle crossings

Holding

  • holding-start: First turning sample of a holding pattern: a loop flown while waiting for permission to continue. Holding patterns
  • holding-end: Last turning sample of the pattern. Carries the holding measurements. Holding patterns

Point merge

A point merge system is an arrival procedure in which aircraft fly along an arc, called a leg, at a fixed distance from a merge point until they are sent directly to it.

  • pms-leg-entry: The aircraft starts flying along a leg. Point merge
  • pms-leg-exit: The aircraft leaves the leg towards the merge point. Carries the point merge measurements. Point merge
  • pms-merge-point: The aircraft passes closest to a merge point, within 3 NM of it. Point merge

Airspace

  • xing-fir: The flight passes from one flight information region (FIR) or upper information region (UIR) to another. FIR crossings

Track limits

  • first_seen: The first position report of the track. First seen and last seen
  • last_seen: The last position report of the track. First seen and last seen

Event types of release v0.0.2 that release v2.0.0 no longer publishes, such as take-off, first-xing-fl{level} and entry-runway, are listed with their replacements on Releases.

Fields of the info column

info holds extra details of an event as JSON text, for example {"apt_icao": "EGLL", "runway": "27R", ...}. The fields depend on the event type; a field without a value is left out. An empty info (an empty text) means the event type has no extra details.

Take-off, landing and other runway events

take-off-roll, ATOT, xing-runway-threshold, ALDT, line-up, runway-vacated, runway-crossing-entry, runway-crossing-vacated:

  • apt_icao: ICAO code of the airport.
  • runway: Runway direction used, for example 27R.
  • rwy_ident: The same, under the name used by earlier releases.
  • runway_bearing_deg: True bearing of the runway centre line, in degrees clockwise from true north.
  • traversal_class: Class of the runway pass: departure, arrival or crossing.
  • align_deg: Angle between the aircraft’s track and the runway, in degrees.
  • max_gs_kt: Highest ground speed during the runway pass, in knots (kt).
  • osn_flight_id: Call sign received during the runway pass.
  • milestone: Label of the moment in the PRU flight diagram (see milestones of a flight): T06 line-up, T07 take-off roll, T08 take-off, T16 threshold, T17 touchdown, T19 runway vacated. The PRU numbered them for this diagram only; they have no official status and differ from the A-CDM Implementation Manual’s milestone numbers. Not set on runway crossings.
  • method: On ATOT and ALDT only: acdm when the time was found on the runway, as above.
  • height_reference: What the height above the ground was measured from: track (the aircraft’s own altitude on the ground at that airport) or elevation (the airport’s published elevation).
  • bracket_s: On ATOT and ALDT only: seconds between the two position reports the 15 ft crossing was placed between.

An ATOT or ALDT that could not be found on the runway is found from the climb or the descent instead (see Take-off and landing times). Its info holds apt_icao, runway and runway_bearing_deg (as above) and:

  • method: legacy.
  • role: departure or arrival.
  • bearing_error_deg: Angle between the aircraft’s median track and the runway, in degrees.
  • n_samples: Number of position reports the time was found from.
  • at_track_edge: true when the report the time comes from is the first report of the track (take-off) or its last (landing).

Go-around

  • apt_icao: ICAO code of the destination airport.
  • osn_flight_id: Call sign received.
  • low_height_ft: Lowest height above the airport during the approach, in feet.
  • recovery_roc_ft_min: Highest rate of climb after that point, in feet per minute.
  • excursion_seconds: Duration of the excursion, in seconds.

Block times

Event type Field Meaning
AOBT stand_exit Time of the exit from the stand this off-block leaves (see Off-block and in-block times). Absent when the part of the track holds no such stand passage.
AOBT stand Name in OpenStreetMap of the stand of stand_exit, when it has one.
AOBT apt_icao ICAO code of the airport of that stand.
AOBT take_off, take_off_method The take-off of the same part of the track, and the method that found it (acdm or legacy).
AIBT stand_entry Time of the entry into the stand this in-block reaches. Absent when the part of the track holds no such stand passage.
AIBT stand Name in OpenStreetMap of the stand of stand_entry, when it has one.
AIBT apt_icao ICAO code of the airport of that stand.
AIBT landing, landing_method The landing of the same part of the track, and the method that found it.

Airport surface

entry-{element} and exit-{element}:

  • osm_id: Identifier of the area in OpenStreetMap, the open map of the world. Where the aircraft enters or leaves several areas of one kind at the same report, the event names the smallest identifier.
  • osm_aeroway: Kind of area in OpenStreetMap, for example taxiway.
  • osm_ref: Name or number of the area in OpenStreetMap, for example a stand number.
  • osm_airport: ICAO code of the airport.
  • opdi_time_in_use_s: Time spent in the area, in seconds.
  • osn_icao24: ICAO 24-bit address of the aircraft.
  • osn_flight_id: Call sign received.
  • at_track_start: true on an entry at the first report with a position of the track: reception started there.
  • at_track_end: true on an exit at the last report with a position of the track: reception stopped there.
  • ground_only: true on the events of a track that never leaves the ground and whose aircraft type is unknown or a vehicle type, in practice an airport vehicle.
  • encloses_stand: true on the passage of a stand area that contains a smaller stand passed at the same time.

Top of climb and top of descent

  • d200_time: Time of the top as first found, before moving.
  • d200_altitude_ft: Altitude of the top as first found, in feet.
  • relocated: true when the top was moved, false otherwise.
  • analysis_radius_nm: Radius of the analysis around the airport, in NM (200).
  • method: pru: the method of the EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit.
  • observed: false when the track shows no altitude at least 3,000 ft below the top before it (top of climb) or after it (top of descent): the top is at the edge of reception.

Level-offs

level-off-climb-start, level-off-climb-end, level-off-descent-start, level-off-descent-end:

  • kpi: ICAO indicator the level-off counts for: KPI17 (climb) or KPI19 (descent).
  • duration_s: Duration of the level-off, in seconds.
  • distance_nm: Distance flown during the level-off, in NM.
  • level_ft: Altitude of the level-off, in feet.

Flight-level crossings

xing-fl{level}:

  • crossing_seq: Number of the crossing of that level on the flight (first = 1).
  • direction: up or down.
  • bracket_s: Seconds between the two position reports the crossing was placed between.

Distance rings

xing-{radius}nm:

  • apt_icao: ICAO code of the airport the circle is drawn around.
  • direction: inbound (towards the airport) or outbound.
  • crossing_seq: Number of the crossing of this circle on the flight (first = 1).
  • bearing: Direction of the crossing point from the airport, in degrees clockwise from true north.
  • flight_level: Flight level of the aircraft at the crossing.
  • bracket_s: As for flight-level crossings.
  • position_jump: true when the two reports the crossing was placed between imply more than 1,000 kt: the position stepped, as near areas of GPS spoofing.

Holding

holding-start and holding-end carry the same fields:

  • holding_seq: Number of the holding pattern on the flight (first = 1).
  • pattern: racetrack or orbit.
  • direction: Direction of turn: R (right) or L (left).
  • circuits: Number of loops: total turn divided by 360 degrees, to one decimal.
  • duration_s: Time in the holding pattern, in seconds.
  • distance_nm: Distance flown in it, in NM.
  • altitude_start_ft: Altitude at the start, in feet.
  • altitude_end_ft: Altitude at the end, in feet.
  • straight_pct: Share of the time flown straight, in percent.
  • context: arrival (the flight lands at its destination within 60 minutes and 150 NM of the end of the hold), en-route (it lands later or further away) or other (local flight, no landing, three or more holds, or holds over half the time in the air).

Point merge

pms-leg-entry and pms-leg-exit carry the same fields:

  • apt_icao: ICAO code of the airport the system serves.
  • pms_id: Identifier of the point merge system.
  • merge_point: Name of the merge point.
  • leg_seq: Number of the leg flown on the flight (first = 1).
  • direction: Direction of flight along the arc: cw (clockwise) or ccw (counter-clockwise).
  • leg_distance_nm: Distance of the leg from the merge point, in NM.
  • leg_level_ft: Altitude on the leg, in feet.
  • duration_s: Time on the leg, in seconds.
  • distance_nm: Distance flown along the leg, in NM.
  • direct_to_distance_nm: Distance to the merge point on leaving the leg, in NM.
  • direct_aligned: true when the aircraft then flew straight to the merge point.

pms-merge-point carries apt_icao, pms_id and merge_point (as above) and:

  • closest_nm: Closest distance to the merge point, in NM.
  • via_leg: true when the aircraft flew a leg of the system just before.

FIR crossings

xing-fir:

  • crossing_seq: Number of the crossing on the flight (first = 1).
  • fir_from: The region left, for example EGTTFIR.
  • fir_to: The region entered.
  • fl: Flight level at the crossing.
  • bracket_s: Time between the last position report in the old region and the first in the new one, in seconds.
  • airac_cfmu: The AIRAC cycle of the boundaries used (524). An AIRAC cycle is the 28-day period in which aeronautical data such as airspace boundaries take effect.
  • airac_validity_start: First day of that cycle.
  • airac_validity_end: Last day of that cycle.
  • vertical: true when the two regions lie one above the other (a lower and an upper region), so the crossing is a climb or descent through their boundary level.

Events without details

level-start, level-end, first_seen and last_seen have an empty info.

Source

source names where the position reports of an event come from: in release v2.0.0 always OSN, the OpenSky Network.

Versions and release

Three columns say which method and release produced a row.

Column Where What it names Values in release v2.0.0
release every row of both files The data release; the same on every row. v2.0.0
version flight list The method that built the flight list row. v6.0.0
flight_version flight events The version of the event’s flight in the flight list. v6.0.0
version flight events The method that produced the event. Different event types can have different versions. A method that changes gets a new version, so older data stay reproducible. see below

Event versions of release v2.0.0:

  • events_v0.4.0: runway events, block times, airport surface, vertical profile, distance rings, first_seen, last_seen
  • holding_v0.2.0: holding-start, holding-end
  • pms_v0.2.0: pms-leg-entry, pms-leg-exit, pms-merge-point
  • fir_v0.2.0: xing-fir

Holding, point merge and FIR write the versions above when at least one of their settings differs from release v0.0.2. A day processed with the release v0.0.2 settings gets holding_v0.1.0, pms_v0.1.0 and fir_v0.1.0, and the flight list versions of that release. The measurement versions below follow the same rule.

The measurement columns have no version column of their own:

  • distance_flown_nm: distance_v0.0.4
  • time_passed_s: time_v0.0.2
  • holding_duration_s, holding_distance_nm, holding_circuits: holding_v0.2.0
  • pms_leg_time_s, pms_leg_distance_nm, pms_direct_to_distance_nm: pms_v0.2.0

The measurements view (see Access) gives each measured value as a row with this version in its version column.

Identifiers and joins

  • flight_id (a flight, that is a track): The first 16 characters of the SHA-256 hash of the aircraft address, an underscore, and the time of the track’s first position in seconds since 1970-01-01 (Unix time), for example 3f9a0c1d2b4e5f60_1781412334.
  • event_id (an event): 32 hexadecimal characters, computed from the flight, the event type, the time and the version of the event. The same event gets the same identifier when a day is processed again.
  • icao24 (an aircraft’s transponder): Six hexadecimal characters, for example 4ca123.
  • flt_id (the call sign): As broadcast, for example DLH123.

Joins:

  • Flight events to flight list: on flight_id. Usually not needed: see Flight events.
  • Flight index to flight list: on flight_id; file names the daily flight list file that holds the flight.
  • Views of the release v0.0.2 shape: events.id is the event_id, measurements.event_id joins to events.id, and events.flight_id joins to flight_list_v0.id (the view and the Python reader both write it as id, in lower case).
  • OpenSky Network data: with icao24, the call sign and the time span from first_seen to last_seen, the position reports of a flight can be fetched from the OpenSky Network’s historical database, for example with the tools on its data tools page.

A flight_id depends on the method that built the track, so identifiers of different releases do not match: data of release v0.0.2 and v2.0.0 cannot be joined on flight_id. Join on icao24, call sign and time instead.

Empty measurement columns

Measurement columns Set on Empty on
distance_flown_nm, time_passed_s nearly every event AOBT, AIBT, the four level-off types, and ATOT and ALDT found from the climb or the descent (method = legacy in info)
holding_duration_s, holding_distance_nm, holding_circuits holding-end every other event type, holding-start included
pms_leg_time_s, pms_leg_distance_nm, pms_direct_to_distance_nm pms-leg-exit every other event type, pms-leg-entry included
